_comment: Fragment 45 — D-92: Lane C's environment. Channel widened, tallies removed, work order written. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-92 — Lane C's Environment Prepared Before Its Phase Opens
nodes.description: The Lane C counterpart of D-90 and D-91: the handoff channel widened to accept Lane C entries, the check tallies removed from four documents, a work order written at .github/WORKFLOWS-SPEC.md, and an entry point installed in Lane C's rule file tail.
nodes.rationale: It did not consist of copying the Lane B work. Two of the four items are defects in controls installed by D-90 and D-91, found only because preparing a second lane exercised them from a direction the first never did.

nodes.label: G74 — a Control Scoped to One Lane Cannot Fail for the Others
nodes.description: Check 10 filtered entry filenames on B- alone, so a C-NNN entry was invisible. The check would report no entries yet with Lane C's blocker sitting in the directory. Filter widened to accept both series, negative-tested in both directions.
nodes.rationale: This is the exact failure the check exists to prevent, aimed at the one lane it did not cover. D-90 reasoned carefully about acknowledged versus answered and not at all about whose entries count. Lane A raises nothing in the channel, so an A- prefix is deliberately excluded.

nodes.label: G75 — the Rule Against Tallies Sat Three Paragraphs Above the Tally
nodes.description: Four documents asserted the number of C-14 checks as a literal and all four were wrong. The build spec was wrong twice in one sentence, saying extended to nine beside a local eight of eight. Tallies removed and replaced with the rule that determines CI coverage: what a check reads.
nodes.rationale: Not fixed by correcting the number, because a corrected number drifts again at the next check. G55, G56 and G58 all record this mechanism, and the two rule files that state it carried a tally three paragraphs later.

nodes.label: Deleting a Tally Silently Deleted Two Tier Claims
nodes.description: Decision anchors travelled inside the sentences carrying the counts. Removing the tallies removed D-83 from all three rule files and D-72 from the verification apparatus spec, regressing two tier claims that had been true for days. tier-sweep caught both, one run apart.
nodes.rationale: Both were fixed by restoring the reference, never by dropping the claim. Recorded because the same thing will happen to anyone deleting prose from a governed document: check what the sentence was anchoring before deleting it.

nodes.label: Lane C's Work Order Sits One Directory Above Its Surface
nodes.description: The two items queued for Lane C existed only as prose inside register sections about other things. Under D-86's principle a build lane is not expected to read the register, so Lane C had no way to learn what it owed. The work order names the surface, what CI may call, the SKIP contract and the queued items.
nodes.rationale: The .github directory minus workflows is Lane A's under D-84, so a spec placed there is single-lane for its author and unmissable for its reader. The same unnamed-location defect G27 carried, now on the execution side.

nodes.label: C-18 — the Job Rename Needs a Paired Act No Lane Owns
nodes.description: The CI job name uses U+00B7 middle dots and GitHub matches a required status check by that exact string. Renaming to ASCII must happen together with the branch-protection rule change, or the required check never reports and every pull request blocks indefinitely.
nodes.rationale: Branch protection is a repository-settings act and no lane owns it. The half-done state fails closed, which is the safe direction and still a stoppage. Lane C raises a blocked-on-decision entry naming both exact strings and waits.

nodes.label: The Tally Removal Was a Prerequisite, Not Tidying
nodes.description: Lane C's first queued item adds fetch-depth zero so source-sweep runs in CI. That changes how many checks run in CI, and four documents asserted that number as a literal.
nodes.rationale: Landing the workflow change first would have made four documents wrong, including both rule files every agent reads first. The parent-child ordering here is a real dependency rather than a presentational one.
